rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Ozone is oxygen with an edge. It occurs as the **stratospheric shield** (15–35 km up, swallowing UV-B/UV-C) and as lightning's after-scent at ground level; the laboratory makes it the same way the sky does — **silent electric discharge** through dry O₂ in a cooled Siemen's ozoniser, 3O₂ ⇌ 2O₃ (+142 kJ), where formation and decomposition fight to a ~10 % steady state.…

rows.text: ***The after-storm smell*** — lightning's discharge converts a sliver of air's O₂ to O₃; the pungent freshness is the molecule announcing its own preparation method.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Sharp-Smelling Shield Ozone (O₃) is oxygen's aggressive allotrope: made by lightning and ozonisers, decomposing back to O₂ with nascent oxygen in hand. This topic covers its occurrence, preparation, bent resonance structure, the starch-iodide test, and its uses — from sterilising water to the stratospheric shield whose depletion is topic 62.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Occurrence - **Stratosphere:** the ozone layer (~15–35 km altitude) absorbs most solar UV-B/UV-C — life's sunscreen. - **Trace ground-level:** after thunderstorms (lightning discharge), around electric motors and copiers, in smog (a pollutant there). ### 2.2 Preparation - **Silent electric discharge ozoniser:** 3O₂ ⇌ 2O₃, ΔH = +142 kJ.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Numbers: 117 degrees, 128 pm, bond order 1.5, +142 kJ, ~10% yield. Bent + resonance + diamagnetic. Test pair: starch-iodide (any oxidant) + turpentine (ozone only). Silent discharge, dry O2, cool electrodes.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Ozone's chemistry is one weak bond: the third oxygen leaves as nascent [O], and every use — sterilising, bleaching, the iodide test — is that leaving in action.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Occurrence: stratospheric ozone layer (15-35 km, UV shield); traces after lightning, in smog. Preparation: silent electric discharge ozoniser, dry O2, cooled electrodes; 3O2 = 2O3, dH = +142 kJ; ~10% steady state (discharge also decomposes O3).…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The Montreal Protocol (1987) phased out CFCs to save the ozone layer — the first universally ratified environmental treaty, and the stratosphere is slowly recovering.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Why must the discharge in an ozoniser be silent rather than sparking?  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions **Ozone's bonds are equal:** drawing one single and one double O–O bond as literal is wrong — resonance makes both bonds identical at 128 pm, order 1.5.  ·  **The starch-iodide test is not ozone-exclusive:** H₂O₂ also liberates iodine; the **turpentine decolourisation** is the discriminating test.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Ozone is good up high, bad down low:** stratospheric O₃ protects; ground-level O₃ is a respiratory irritant and smog component — same molecule, opposite reputations.  ·  ## 7.
